headline: Sellers Dominated From Open to Close as Breadth Collapsed Across Nearly Every Corner of the Market
body_html:
Thursday's session offered little shelter. Of the 545 names tracked across our universe, only 128 finished in positive territory while 416 closed lower — a lopsided retreat that underscored how broadly the selling pressure spread. Every sector in our coverage ended the day in the red, with Software managing the shallowest decline at 0.37%, while Homebuilders bore the deepest damage, surrendering 2.34% by the closing bell. Industrials, Materials, and Consumer names each fell well over a percent, confirming this was not a rotation but a broad-based markdown.

The lone pocket of genuine strength was concentrated in RF and audio chip names tied to the Apple supply chain. Skyworks Solutions surged nearly 10% — the session's standout mover — after a new analyst endorsement drew fresh attention to a name that had fallen out of favour. Qorvo and Cirrus Logic followed with gains of 6.77% and 5.2%, respectively, suggesting investors interpreted the analyst call as a catalyst for the entire Apple-adjacent semiconductor group. Academy Sports + Outdoors added nearly 6%, a quiet outlier in an otherwise punished consumer tape.

The macro backdrop grew no quieter after the close. Fresh U.S. sanctions on networks supporting Iranian proxy forces, combined with reports of Iran producing new missiles and Houthi advances near the Red Sea, kept geopolitical risk elevated — a headwind energy traders are pricing in even as the broad sector itself slipped 0.75% on the day. Diesel crossing six dollars per gallon for the first time only added to cost-pressure anxieties already weighing on industrials and transport-exposed names. Thursday served as a reminder that when breadth is this poor, even compelling individual stories struggle to move the needle.

briefs.headline: Skyworks Surges Nearly 10% After Analyst Reversal Sparks Apple-Chain Rally
briefs.body: Skyworks Solutions led the entire market on Thursday, jumping 9.79% after a new analyst endorsement reframed the investment case for the RF chipmaker. The call rippled through related names: Qorvo gained 6.77% and Cirrus Logic climbed 5.2%, making Apple-adjacent semiconductors the session's clearest bright spot in an otherwise deeply negative tape.

briefs.headline: American Eagle Plunges 14%, Dragging Apparel Peers Lower
briefs.body: American Eagle Outfitters was Thursday's worst performer, tumbling 13.97% in the steepest single-session decline across our coverage universe. Abercrombie & Fitch fell 6.02% in sympathy, compressing the consumer-apparel group further at a time when the broader Consumer sector was already down 1.46% on the day.

briefs.headline: Diesel Tops Six Dollars a Gallon for the First Time, Fanning Inflation Concerns
briefs.body: The U.S. average diesel price crossed the six-dollar-per-gallon threshold for the first time, according to GasBuddy data reported by Reuters. The milestone adds tangible cost pressure to freight, manufacturing, and agricultural supply chains, and may complicate the Federal Reserve's inflation calculus heading into the fall policy calendar.

briefs.headline: U.S. Sanctions Target Iran Proxy Networks Amid Escalating Middle East Tensions
briefs.body: Washington imposed new sanctions Thursday on financial networks accused of supporting Iranian proxy forces across the Middle East, Reuters reported. The action came alongside separate reporting that Iran is assembling new missiles in limited quantities and that Houthi forces — aided by Iranian arms and counsel — have seized a strategically significant Red Sea city.

briefs.headline: OpenAI Takes Aim at Junior Banker Workloads With Finance-Focused ChatGPT Offering
briefs.body: OpenAI launched a version of ChatGPT tailored specifically for financial-services workflows, directly targeting the research, summarisation, and analysis tasks that occupy Wall Street's junior analyst ranks. The move marks an escalation in AI competition for professional services revenue and adds pressure on traditional financial data and software providers.

briefs.headline: UAE Commits €40 Billion to Germany While Regional Diplomatic Rifts Widen
briefs.body: The United Arab Emirates pledged €40 billion in investment across Germany as part of a package of bilateral business agreements, Reuters reported. The announcement arrived on the same day Algeria severed diplomatic ties with the UAE, illustrating the fractured state of Gulf and North African geopolitics that continues to ripple through commodity and emerging-market sentiment.
